body:
I’ve recently revised OWASP ASVS v4.0.3, and I would like to propose an improvement to V1 – Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling.

In the current version, sections 1.1.1 through 1.1.7 consistently use the term “Verify” (e.g., Verify that threat modeling is performed…). While this is important from a validation standpoint, I noticed there is no clear guidance or structure (except the cheat sheets) on how to create or maintain a solid Threat Modeling documentation/report.

I’d like to suggest adding a practical walkthrough or minimum criteria for what constitutes solid threat modeling documentation. (to have points as ensure to follow these or ensure following this Guideline and then to Verify if the Threat modeling is providing the intended output. 
for example, to have simple walkthrough for threat modeling documentation like:

1- System Description
Brief description of the system, components, technologies, and boundaries.

2- Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs)
Visual representation of how data moves within the system, including trust boundaries.

3- Threat Identification
Using models like STRIDE, LINDDUN, or Kill Chain to identify potential threats.

4- Threat Prioritization
Use scoring methods such as DREAD or CVSS to evaluate risk levels.

5- Mitigations and Controls Mapping
Document how identified threats are mitigated, including linkage to ASVS controls.

6- Residual Risk
Highlight risks that remain unaddressed or accepted.

7- Review & Update Frequency
State how frequently the model is updated (e.g., during major design changes).

adding to it , we might ensure the coverage of  open source library ( as threat entery point ), and having SBOM inventory  ( which is getting lots of heat lately for Compliance purposes

Hi, we are preparing release candidate for v5.0 and from this most of the threat-modeling related requirements are removed.

At the same time, the threat modeling in the background is still required in a way, and we ask some "documented security decisions" in v5.0 to address those concerns you pointed out.

At the moment, please be sure you are reading the most up to date version:
* https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/tree/master/5.0/en

Alternative output:
* https://asvs.dev/v5.0.draft/0x00-Header/

thank you for your clarification, will review the newer version 5.0 as you mentioned,
however, shouldn't be done as appendix or additional section for having a Threat model for your application, and enhancing it to have Threat landscape for this application and have SBOM, as they are highlighted in many compliance nowadays, and i know some Governing Entities in some countries are requesting it, so wouldn't be valuable ? 
i know it is mentioned in  V15 Coding ,
but what i mean is , detailed information on how to implement , not just verify .  :)

and apologies for any inconvenience 

> Hi, we are preparing release candidate for v5.0 and from this most of the threat-modeling related requirements are removed.
> 
> At the same time, the threat modeling in the background is still required in a way, and we ask some "documented security decisions" in v5.0 to address those concerns you pointed out.
> 
> At the moment, please be sure you are reading the most up to date version:
> 
> * https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/tree/master/5.0/en
> 
> Alternative output:
> 
> * https://asvs.dev/v5.0.draft/0x00-Header/

> but what i mean is , detailed information on how to implement , not just verify . :)

"Verification" is literally written into the ASVS name and this is also how we are scoping things. ASVS contains (only) security requirements that are verifiable.

"How to implement" topics we watch to belong to Cheat Sheet Series project and there is no need to overlap.

To conclude that, from ASVS v5.0 we removed requirements to just ask threat modeling to be done. In development lifecycle it is important step to do but we can not improve application security _only_ because threat modeling is done - we need to verify that it is implemented and this is what ASVS is about - what is done with the application.

There are some things that we need from threat modeling - those are security decisions without which you can not implement or verify certain security aspects.

Instead of quite abstract:
> 2- Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs)
> Visual representation of how data moves within the system, including trust boundaries.

We have requirements in section V13.1 to cover that more precisely.

As I can not see any action to take from this issue, I'll close this out. I hope that this description explained more, what the ASVS is and what is required to have a requirement in ASVS.

I just want to mention that the entire leadership team at ASVS supports this. @elarlang is spot on correct here.

But you may want to author a different threat modeling standard that looks like ASVS. You can submit a new project proposal to OWASP if you want to take this on.

title: suggestion regarding Threat modeling in ASVS
